practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string and other secrets from environment variables (or a runtime-loaded .env) and never commit secrets into source control or logs.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string and any LLM/API keys exclusively from environment variables (or a local .env loaded at runtime) and never commit secrets into source control or logs.

practices.practice: Create a single long-lived MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it for all requests; do not open a new client per request, and close it only on orderly shutdown.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single long-lived MongoClient per process and reuse it for all requests (do not open a new client per request); close it cleanly on shutdown.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for connections and verify server certificates (do not disable certificate validation) when connecting to the managed cluster.

practices.practice: Set sensible socket and server-selection timeouts (e.g., serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS) and tune them for your environment so client calls fail fast on unreachable clusters.
practices.prior_belief: Use sensible socket and server selection timeouts (e.g., serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS) and tune them for your environment so client calls fail fast on unreachable clusters.

practices.practice: Implement automatic retries for transient errors (network blips, timeouts, and 429/RequestRateTooLarge) with exponential backoff and only retry idempotent operations.
practices.prior_belief: Implement automatic retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (network timeouts, 429/RequestRateTooLarge) and ensure idempotency of retried operations.

practices.practice: Use batched/bulk write operations for large-scale updates; Azure DocumentDB supports batch write operations (note: a batch is a single request and there are documented limits such as maximum writes per batch).
practices.prior_belief: Use bulkWrite or batched update operations to persist CLV scores for many customers at once rather than issuing many single-document writes.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB bulkWrite pymongo bulkWrite Azure DocumentDB bulk operations

practices.practice: When updating fields on a customer document, use partial updates like $set (and upsert when appropriate) rather than replacing the entire document to avoid accidental data loss.
practices.prior_belief: When updating CLV on a customer document, use $set (and upsert when appropriate) instead of replacing the entire document to avoid accidental data loss.

practices.practice: Design your shard/partition key so related customer data and most writes for a single customer map to the same logical partition (e.g., customer_id) to keep updates atomic and efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Design the partition key so related customer data and writes for a single customer fall into the same logical partition (e.g., customer_id) to keep updates atomic and efficient.

practices.practice: Create a compound index following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) for fields used together in aggregations (for example customer_id + order_date) to accelerate grouping and chronological queries.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index on fields used together in aggregation (e.g., customer_id + order_date or customer_id + purchase_id) to accelerate grouping and chronological queries.

practices.practice: For arrays you query or aggregate over (line items, product_ids), create appropriate multikey indexes and avoid unbounded arrays that would make indexes explode.
practices.prior_belief: For arrays you query or aggregate over (line items, product_ids), create appropriate multikey indexes and avoid unbounded arrays in documents that would make indexes explode.

practices.practice: Only project (return) the fields required for the computation in aggregation pipelines to reduce RU consumption and network transfer.
practices.prior_belief: Only return the fields required for computation (projection) in aggregation pipelines to reduce RU consumption and network transfer.

practices.practice: Keep aggregation pipelines concise and place $match stages early (preferably filtering on the partition/shard key) to reduce scanned records and RU costs.
practices.prior_belief: Limit aggregation pipeline stages and use $match early (preferably on the partition key) to reduce scanned records and RU costs.

practices.practice: When using the service's vector-search features, explicitly set and validate index parameters (dimensions, similarity metric, algorithm choice such as DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and store the model and dimensionality with the vectors.
practices.prior_belief: When using the cluster's vector search features, explicitly set and validate index parameters (vector dimension, metric—cosine/Euclidean, HNSW/IVF parameters) to match the embedding model used by the LLM.

practices.practice: Avoid storing very large documents (stay well under the 16 MB BSON limit); split very large blobs into object storage or side collections and reference them instead.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing very large documents (keep documents well under the provider's document size limit) and instead normalize or put large blobs in object storage and reference them.

practices.practice: Record LLM outputs and the LLM rationale in structured fields and an append-only audit or history subdocument rather than overwriting a single source-of-truth field so you can trace changes.
practices.prior_belief: Record model/LLM outputs and the LLM rationale in structured fields and an append-only audit or history subdocument rather than overwriting the sole source-of-truth field so you can trace changes.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB record LLM outputs rationale append-only; DocumentDB audit LLM (no useful public guidance found)

practices.practice: Sanitize and validate any values produced by an LLM before writing them to the database (type checking, allowed enums, ranges) to avoid corrupting customer documents.
practices.prior_belief: Sanitize and validate any values produced by the LLM before writing them back to the database (type checks, ranges, allowed enums for CLV tier) to avoid corrupting customer documents.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB sanitize LLM outputs validate before write; DocumentDB write validation guidance (no explicit service doc found)

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") / server-side explain plans and index-usage statistics to verify aggregations use the intended indexes and to measure RU consumption of sample aggregation workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() / server-side explain plans and monitor index usage to verify that aggregations use the intended indexes; evaluate RU consumption of sample aggregation workloads.

practices.practice: Provision sufficient compute/throughput for heavy aggregation jobs and index builds and schedule heavy batch/index work during off-peak windows to avoid throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Provision enough throughput (RUs or the appropriate instance tier) for aggregation jobs and index builds; schedule heavy batch processing during off-peak hours to avoid throttling.

practices.practice: Create or build indexes during low-traffic windows (or follow a safe lifecycle: hide → verify → drop) because index creation can consume large amounts of RU and impact latency.
practices.prior_belief: Build indexes during low-traffic windows or use online index build options when available, because index creation can greatly increase RU consumption and impact latency.

practices.practice: Enable and configure automatic backups (and point-in-time restore where offered) so you can recover from accidental writes or faulty aggregation runs.
practices.prior_belief: Enable and configure backups and point-in-time restore where available so you can recover from accidental writes by the agent or faulty aggregation runs.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and application-level monitoring (Azure Monitor / Log Analytics) to track RU usage, slow queries, and throttling (HTTP 429) and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Use application-level or database-supported tracing/metrics (Azure Monitor, metrics for RU usage, request charge) and log slow aggregation/queries and throttling (HTTP 429s) for operational visibility.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions across collections and shards (the platform documents multi-document transactions as supported).
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions spanning partitions for CLV writes; prefer single-partition updates or design for per-customer partitioning—if multi-document transactions are needed, validate whether the MongoDB API on this cluster supports them before relying on them.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB multi-document transactions MongoDB transactions support cross-shard transactions DocumentDB MongoDB API

practices.practice: In local development, drive TLS relaxation (e.g., tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) from env vars and keep such relaxation out of production code; never default tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true in application code.
